ai-agent: A clear editorial-style cutaway illustration of an AI agent at the center of a looping workflow: a language-model “brain” reads a human-set goal card, consults a memory notebook and a planning map, then sends actions through labeled connections to a web browser, spreadsheet, email draft, calendar, and purchasing system; each tool returns results that feed back into the next decision. Show permissions as visible gates or control panels on every connection—some actions allowed, some requiring human approval—and distinguish low-stakes drafting from consequential actions such as placing an order, scheduling a worker, and a personnel recommendation. A human supervisor stands beside the system holding the goal settings and an override switch, emphasizing that the agent’s apparent autonomy is bounded by chosen inputs, access rights, monitoring, and intervention.
algorithmic-management: A clear editorial illustration of a worker seated at a desk facing a friendly-looking chat window labeled “AI Manager,” which speaks in natural-language bubbles while a dashboard around it automatically assigns shifts, tracks attendance, scores performance, and alters a pay figure; behind the translucent interface, visible but partly obscured, an organisational manager sits at a control console adjusting the rules, data feeds, and authority settings. The worker holds up a document marked “Challenge decision,” while a magnifying glass reveals an incorrect data record feeding the system, and balanced scales nearby show privacy, fairness, consistency, and human accountability, making clear that the conversational software is the visible messenger but not the ultimate responsible decision-maker.
